data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Software is deterministic; human panels are stochastic."],"overturn_conditions":["If negative tests are found to be logically inconsistent with the positive ones."],"shared_structure":["Positive tests verify the system works as intended.","Negative tests verify the system doesn't work when it shouldn't."],"source_memory_refs":["General Software Testing"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a suite of passing positive tests doesn't prove code correctness (it could be a hardcoded return), a panel reaching the right answer doesn't prove reliability without negative tests."]},"claim":"Genuine reliability gain is distinguished from 'outcome tracking' by the presence of 'Negative Constraint Validation'\u2014the panel's ability to correctly reject a result when a checklist 'decoy' or 'negative trigger' is present, even if the final answer seems plausible.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The 'decoy' is so obvious it doesn't test the actual cognitive process.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel is coached on the specific nature of the decoy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the panel correctly marks 'No' on a check for a condition that *should not* be present (per SCR_001), it proves they are executing the logical constraints of the checklist rather than simply checking boxes to reach a known or guessed correct outcome.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
